title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Companion mode that detects, a web extension that delivers
summary: Kotlin Jump 1.42.12 looks at the web extension and the indexing pipeline. Companion mode never detected the JetBrains Kotlin extension, the dead-code family published its findings on phantom paths on github.dev, a dozen providers were advertised on the web with nothing behind them, and Re-index silently dropped the bundled stdlib.

highlights.title: Companion mode finally detects JetBrains
highlights.description: companionMode: auto looked for JetBrains.kotlin-lsp, an id that never existed, so with the JetBrains Kotlin extension installed every provider was registered twice: doubled hovers, two outline groups, duplicate hints. The real ids are checked, and the status bar says "· companion".

highlights.title: Dead code that shows up on github.dev
highlights.description: Findings were published on file:// paths rebuilt from fsPath, which point nowhere on the web: phantom entries in Problems, no squiggles, quick fixes reading a missing file. The editor's own URIs are used now, and a dozen desktop-only providers join the web extension.

highlights.title: Re-index keeps the stdlib
highlights.description: Re-index cleared the bundled stdlib with everything else and never reloaded it: Cmd+Click on listOf answered "No definition found" until a reload. It also re-reads excludePatterns and maxIndexedFiles, which the watchers now follow live too.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Warns when kotlinJump.maxIndexedFiles caps the index, and keeps the status bar counter current after a checkout or a deleted file.
Adds the androidx.annotation.VisibleForTesting import with the annotation, and clears a detector's warnings as soon as its setting goes off.
